title: Add live-query health probes and guided mitigation CLI
author: Priya Raman
description: Motivation: During incidents engineers frequently run ad-hoc queries (k8s describe, recent-error-tail, quick-sli checks) to validate hypotheses. This PR adds two coordinated features: 1) a lightweight live-query probe subsystem that can execute predefined, parameterized queries against supported backends (k8s API, metrics API, log tail) and return sanitized short-form results; 2) an interactive guided-mitigation CLI that surfaces curated playbook steps, runs optional probes, and can optionally execute safe remediation steps via the existing playbook-runner. Goals: reduce cognitive overhead for first responders, speed up hypothesis validation, and centralize audit/sanitization for ad-hoc diagnostics. Key design points: - Probes are declarative YAML snippets stored in config and validated at startup. Each probe declares required permissions, estimated cost (timeout/IO), and a sanitizer pipeline. - Live probes run in constrained sandboxes with concurrency/rate limits and per-incident quotas to avoid causing load during high traffic. - The guided CLI is a TUI (fallback to non-interactive mode) that recommends next steps based on incident tags and probe outputs; it supports dry-run and a single-step auto-apply mode gated by RBAC and an explicit approve token. - All probe outputs are scrubbed by a pluggable sanitizer chain and emit only short summaries to the chat/pager context; full sanitized artefacts are attached to the incident record and stored in the audit-log with retention controls. Changes in this PR: - New subsystem: internal/probes with probe executor, validators, and sanitizer registry. - CLI entry: cmd/ibctl/guided_mitigation.go implements interactive flow and non-interactive flags. - Incident adapter: incident/plugins/live_probe_adapter.go to wire probes into incident runbooks and responder actions. - Config: config/probes.yaml.example and feature flag gating (feature.live_probes.enabled). - Docs: docs/diagnostics/live-probes.md and runbook examples in docs/templates/guided-mitigation.md. - Tests: unit tests for sanitizers and integration tests exercising k8s-mock probe runner. Backwards compatibility and safety: feature gated by default, requires explicit operator opt-in for production. Probes that can modify state are opt-in and require a secondary approval token. Checklist: - [x] Implement probe executor and sanitizer registry - [x] CLI flow + dry-run support - [x] Integration tests (mock backends) - [x] Docs and example probes - [x] RBAC and quota checks - [x] Feature gate behind config flag Usage notes: ibctl guided-mitigation --incident=INC-1234 --run-probes --auto-apply=false will launch the TUI, run safe probes, and present ranked playbook steps. See docs/diagnostics/live-probes.md for authoring probes and sanitizer examples. Related: ENG-8123 (reduce MTTI for first-response), SRE-204 (runbook library schema).
